summary: PR D of the stack crates import adds, switched off, the pipelines that will publish @cipherstash/auth with its six napi platform packages to npm (release.yml auth-artifacts/publish-auth via the new reusable _build-auth-artifacts.yml) and stack-auth/stack-profile to crates.io (release-plz.yml crates-armed/release-crates), plus a manual auth-preflight.yml dry run. The release gate gains a separate `auth` flag so an unpublished auth version no longer reads as `js`. The inertness claim holds on reading: both npm jobs need the gate to succeed and report auth=true, which a frozen auth package cannot do, and crates-armed reads the @cipherstash/auth FROZEN_PUBLISHERS entry; script tests covering this ran and passed in CI. Merging this PR therefore publishes nothing. The risk is latent and lands at PR E, when the entries are deleted: the new build differs from the repository's proven FFI native build in two ways that matter. The linux-x64-musl leg sets no `-C target-feature=-crt-static`, under which rustc drops the cdylib crate type, so the leg most likely fails and blocks every JS release on that push; and the gnu legs build on Ubuntu 24.04 runners with no glibc floor, where the FFI line pins glibc 2.28, so the published binaries may not load on older Linux distributions used by @cipherstash/stack consumers. Neither binary check is on the publish path; the preflight that checks architecture and libc is dispatch-only, cannot be run until merged, and does not test glibc version or musl loading.

behaviour_changes.description: The release gate's classify() reports a separate `auth` flag for any unpublished name starting with @cipherstash/auth, removes those names from `js`, and writes `auth=` to GITHUB_OUTPUT; release.yml's gate job exports it.

release.yml gains auth-artifacts (calls _build-auth-artifacts.yml) and publish-auth (npm publish with provenance of six platform tarballs then the wrapper, tags and a GitHub release), both conditioned on production mode and gate auth=true; the `release` (changeset publish) job now also requires publish-auth success whenever auth=true.

New reusable _build-auth-artifacts.yml builds six napi binaries (one matrix leg per platform, on GitHub-hosted runners) and the wasm wrapper, packs seven tarballs and verifies names, file presence and wrapper peer versions, but not binary architecture, libc or loadability.

release-plz.yml gains crates-armed (runs `eql-pipeline-armed.mjs crates`, armed when @cipherstash/auth is absent from FROZEN_PUBLISHERS) and release-crates (release-plz release on the root workspace with OIDC trusted publishing, GPG signing, contents: write); new release-plz.toml publishes only stack-auth and stack-profile in one version group; the workflow now also triggers on root Cargo/release-plz/cliff changes.

New dispatch-only auth-preflight.yml builds the seven tarballs, checks each binary's architecture with `file` and glibc NEEDED entries with readelf, and smoke-loads only the linux-x64-gnu pair on ubuntu-latest. It has no publish credentials.

.changeset/config.json puts the seven auth packages in one fixed group; the seven auth manifests gain repository.directory (needed for npm provenance). package.json is excluded from the frozen-bytes check, so the manifest edit does not trip the gate.
New and extended script tests: auth classification, crates line arming, the auth build workflow's flags and matrix, release-plz root config, repository URLs, lint target lists.

failure_scenarios.title: linux-gnu auth binaries built on Ubuntu 24.04 with no glibc floor fail to load on older Linux
failure_scenarios.trigger: PR E arms the line; a version of @cipherstash/auth is published by publish-auth; a customer on a distribution with an older glibc (e.g. Debian 11, RHEL/Alma 8, Amazon Linux 2) installs @cipherstash/stack or @cipherstash/auth.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: _build-auth-artifacts.yml builds linux-x64-gnu on ubuntu-latest and linux-arm64-gnu on ubuntu-24.04-arm with plain `napi build --target <triple>` (lines 45-53, 112-116), so symbol versions are taken from the runner's glibc. The repository's FFI native line deliberately builds gnu targets through cargo-zigbuild with `--target <triple>.2.28` to pin the glibc floor (_build-ffi-artifacts.yml:240-244, ffi-release-matrix.mjs:59-60). The auth preflight only checks that libc.so.6 is NEEDED and smoke-loads on ubuntu-latest, which has the same glibc as the build host, so a raised floor passes every check.
failure_scenarios.consequence: require('@cipherstash/auth') throws `GLIBC_2.xx not found` at load time for those customers, breaking @cipherstash/stack (and cli, wizard) at runtime. npm publishes are irreversible; recovery is a new release built with a floor. Whether earlier versions published from cipherstash-suite supported these distributions is unknown.

existing_verification.description: auth-preflight.yml checks the gnu binaries link libc.so.6 and smoke-loads linux-x64-gnu on ubuntu-latest; dispatch-only and not run for this change.

missing_verification: A check of the maximum GLIBC_* symbol version required by each gnu binary (e.g. objdump -T) against a stated floor.

failure_scenarios.mitigation: Build the gnu legs with a pinned glibc floor as the FFI line does (cargo-zigbuild `<triple>.2.28`, or a manylinux-style container), and add a max-GLIBC-version assertion to the build or preflight; confirm the floor matches what cipherstash-suite previously shipped.

failure_scenarios.title: linux-x64-musl leg built without -crt-static: cdylib dropped, auth build fails and blocks the JS release
failure_scenarios.trigger: First armed run of auth-artifacts (or the first preflight dispatch) after merge.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The musl leg installs musl-tools and runs `napi build --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` with no RUSTFLAGS (_build-auth-artifacts.yml:54-56, 68-73, 112-116); neither cargo config sets crt-static for musl (root .cargo/config.toml covers wasm only; the auth one covers macOS only). Rust's musl targets default to crt-static, under which rustc drops the cdylib crate type, so no .node is produced (this rustc behaviour is from general knowledge, not run here). The FFI line sets `RUSTFLAGS=-C target-feature=-crt-static` for exactly this target (_build-ffi-artifacts.yml:236-238). The `mv` of stack-auth-node.linux-x64-musl.node then fails, auth-artifacts fails, publish-auth is skipped, and `release` requires publish-auth success when auth=true (release.yml:471-482).
failure_scenarios.consequence: Fails closed: nothing auth is published, but the changeset publish for every other JS package on that push is also skipped until the workflow is fixed and re-run. If instead a statically linked musl module were produced, it would pass the preflight's musl check (which only asserts no glibc NEEDED) while possibly failing to load on Alpine; that variant would be high impact.

failure_scenarios.title: Publish path ships platform binaries without the architecture/libc/load checks the preflight performs
failure_scenarios.trigger: Any mis-built platform binary (wrong arch on a cross-compiled leg such as darwin-x64 on arm64 macos-latest, wrong libc, a module missing exports) once the line is armed, with no preflight dispatched for that version.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: _build-auth-artifacts.yml verifies only the tarball name and that the expected .node filename exists (lines 145-164); publish-auth publishes what it downloads (release.yml:362-418). The architecture, readelf and smoke checks exist only in auth-preflight.yml, which is manual and not a `needs` of publish-auth.
failure_scenarios.consequence: A broken platform package is published irreversibly and breaks @cipherstash/auth (and @cipherstash/stack) on that platform until a new release.
